text:
maria_corp: Hey @support, we're seeing a weird MFA loop after enabling device-trust on our org. Users authenticate via SSO, enroll device trust, then within ~5-10m some users get prompted for MFA again even though their session cookie is still valid. No obvious 401s in the app, just repeated reauth prompts.

alex_support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you share repro steps and any logs you have? Is this across browsers or a single one?

maria_corp: Repro steps: 1) Login via SSO -> complete MFA -> enroll device trust. 2) App (embedded SDK in an iframe) continues to work. 3) After a few minutes, user sees "re-auth required" modal, SDK calls /authorize and we get redirect to IDP. Happens on Chrome and Safari, intermittent (maybe 30% of sessions).

maria_corp: Attaching a snippet from our console logs: 
```
[2026-03-17T14:12:10Z] INFO session: session_cookie present (sid=xxx), device_assertion present
[2026-03-17T14:17:08Z] WARN auth: device_assertion_expired for sid=xxx, prompting reauth
```

maria_corp: Also decoded the device_assertion JWT and saw: 
```
{"sub":"device:abc123","iat":2704838800,"exp":2704839120}
```
Which looks like a 5m TTL. Our session cookie exp is ~3600s.

alex_support: That exp definitely looks short. Two quick Qs: 1) Is the device_assertion coming from your IDP or minted by Redwood? 2) Do you have any proxy that might be rewriting cookies?

maria_corp: The assertion is from the IDP (we use SAML->OIDC bridge) — the timestamp on the assertion matches idp logs. No proxy rewriting.

jordan_oncall: I'm digging through infra logs for the tenant. I can see repeated /authorize calls followed by 302 to the idp. No 500s. Looks like Redwood-side accepts the session cookie but the SDK validates device_assertion freshness separately and forces reauth when exp < now. Could be TTL mismatch between IDP and SDK config.

sam_identity: We rolled a change to the IDP connector yesterday morning that tightened assertion TTL defaults to 5m for device assertions (security hardening). That explains the 5m exp. Previously it was 1h. We can either lengthen assertion TTL on the IDP or make the SDK accept a longer skew/refresh flow.

ryan_eng: Two options for a quick mitigation: 1) Configure IDP to set device_assertion exp closer to session TTL (recommended), or 2) enable SDK param device_assertion_refresh=true so we attempt a silent refresh before falling back to full reauth. I can add the SDK param in a patch and cut a canary today.

maria_corp: Option 2 would be ideal for us short-term because we can't change IDP config (managed by separate infra team). Is the SDK param already present?

ryan_eng: Not in stable yet. I'll do a canary release to eng-runtime that adds device_assertion_refresh with a default backoff window of 60s. If assertion expiry <= 120s we will trigger a silent refresh call to /auth/refresh-device rather than full redirect.

alex_support: Thanks. Jordan — can you coordinate a quick canary rollout for maria's tenant (low traffic window)? Sam, we'll need a heads-up if IDP rotates anything else.

jordan_oncall: Scheduling canary now for tenant maria-corp at 02:00 UTC. I'll watch auth metrics and error rate.

deploy-bot: [02:00 UTC] deploy started: eng-runtime@device-assertion-refresh-canary -> canary-slot-7

deploy-bot: [02:02 UTC] deploy success: eng-runtime@device-assertion-refresh-canary -> canary-slot-7

ryan_eng: Canary live. SDK will attempt silent refresh when assertion exp < 120s. We also log a new metric auth.device_assertion.silent_refresh.{success,failure}.

maria_corp: Confirming after canary rollout: users who previously hit rapid reauth are now kept in app, no full redirect. Looks good on Chrome. :thumbsup:

jordan_oncall: Metrics: device_assertion.silent_refresh.success = 86% for maria-corp tenant during canary, full-redirects down 78%. No backend errors.

sam_identity: We'll follow up with the IDP team to discuss default TTLs for device assertions — security tradeoff vs UX. I'll propose a 30m default or allow per-tenant override.

alex_support: Great outcome. I'll mark this thread as escalated->resolved and file a short postmortem with steps: cause = IDP tightened device_assertion TTL; mitigation = SDK silent refresh; long-term = IDP config change/per-tenant TTL.

maria_corp: Thanks everyone — appreciate the fast turnaround. If you push the param to stable we can flip it on permanently.

ryan_eng: Will do. I'll open a PR to merge canary -> stable and include a feature flag so we can disable per-tenant if needed.

maria_corp: closing the loop — all good now.
